rationale: fastdiff_flow_pixel_constrained-claude-agentic: image_size=512, pixel_spacing=0.3516, n_angles=128, n_det=1024, det_spacing=0.35754, sod=500.0, sdd=1000.0, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.5, train_n=400, val_n=200, noise_i0=100000.0, noise_sigma_e=10.0, seed=42, fd_recon_ckpt=/cluster/maier/Agent4CT/checkpoints/fast_diffusion_pixel_constrained.pt, fd_recon_steps=8, fd_recon_init=fbp, fd_recon_init_t=0.3, fd_recon_eta=1.0, fd_recon_dc=1, fd_recon_dc_n_cg=5, fd_recon_dc_relax=0.5, rationale=iter-2 EXPLORATORY, single knob fd_recon_init_t 0.7->0.3 from iter-1 base. SIX-BOX: (1)PRIOR iter-1 hr=0.0: recon val_rmse=0.01366 vs 128-view FBP baseline rmse=0.00521 (ssim 0.775 vs 0.920, psnr 27.96 vs 36.32dB) -> the Mayo-trained flow prior transferred cross-dataset to breast DEGRADES the already-strong sparse-view breast FBP (2.6x worse RMSE). (2)FAILURE MODE: cross-dataset prior DRIFT - starting the flow high on the schedule (init_t=0.7) lets the mismatched Mayo prior repaint breast structure poorly, pulling RMSE far above the FBP it initialized from. (3)ONE KNOB: fd_recon_init_t 0.7->0.3 (start much closer to FBP; only steps/DC held). (4)HYPOTHESIS: a lower init_t preserves the strong 128-view FBP PSNR while the cross-dataset prior only lightly denoises, and full CG data-consistency re-anchors to the measured sinogram, so RMSE drops toward the baseline and hr moves off 0. (5)BUDGET: iter-1 sampled 200 slices in ~178s (<<20min); lower init_t = fewer effective Euler steps, still fast. (6)Loop continues; iter-3 self-dispatched on landing. Reserved knobs: fd_recon_dc_relax, fd_recon_steps, fd_recon_eta.
